questions.question:
A sender S sends a message m to receiver R, which is digitally signed by S with its private key. In this scenario, one or more of the following security violations can take place.

I. S can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message.
II. A third party attacker can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message
III. R can launch a birthday attack to replace m with a fraudulent message.

Which of the following are possible security violations?
questions.explanation:
A birthday attack finds two messages with the same hash. Only the signer S can use it: S signs a harmless message and later claims the signature was for the other one with the same hash. A third party or R cannot create S's signature on a new hash.

Answer: I only

m1: Send an email from a mail client to a mail server
m2: Download an email from mailbox server to a mail client
m3: Checking email in a web browser

Which is the application level protocol used in each activity?

options.C: m1: SMTP m2: POP m3: HTTP

- Mailbox to client (downloading): POP

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the functionality of an IP based router.

I. A router does not modify the IP packets during forwarding.
II. It is not necessary for a router to implement any routing protocol.
III. A router should reassemble IP fragments if the MTU of the outgoing link is larger than the size of the incoming IP packet.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- I: a router changes the packet (TTL decrement, checksum, possibly fragmentation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: a router can work with static routes only, without any routing protocol [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: routers never reassemble fragments; only the destination does [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: II only

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the slow start phase of the TCP congestion control algorithm. Note that [latex]cwnd[/latex] stands for the TCP congestion window and MSS denotes the Maximum Segment Size.

(i) The cwnd increases by 2 MSS on every successful acknowledgment.
(ii) The cwnd approximately doubles on every successful acknowledgement.
(iii) The cwnd increases by 1 MSS every round trip time.
(iv) The cwnd approximately doubles every round trip time.

Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation:
In slow start, cwnd grows by 1 MSS for each ACK. In one RTT a full window of segments is acknowledged, so cwnd roughly doubles every RTT. Only (iv) is right.

Answer: Only (iv) is true

questions.question: In an Ethernet local area network,which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: A station stops to sense the channel once it starts transmitting a frame.
options.B: The purpose of the jamming signal is to pad the frames that are smaller than the minimum framesize.
options.C: A station continues to transmit the packet even after the collision is detected.
options.D:
The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collisionon
retransmissions.

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- A station keeps sensing while transmitting (that is how it detects collisions) False
- The jam signal tells everyone a collision happened; padding is something else False
- After a collision the station stops transmitting False
- Exponential backoff makes stations wait random, growing times, so they are less likely to collide again True

Answer: The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collision on retransmissions

questions.question: Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of 1 Gbps (= [latex]10^{9} [/latex] bits-per-second). The session starts with a sequence number of 1234. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is _______.
questions.explanation:
TCP numbers bytes with 32-bit sequence numbers, so they wrap after [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes.
Time = [latex]\frac{2^{32}\times8}{10^9}\approx34.36[/latex] s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 34 s.

Answer: 34

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about
the OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocol used in the Internet?

options.A: OSPF implements Bellman-Ford algorithm to find shortest paths.
options.B: OSPF uses Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm to implement least-cost path routing
options.C: OSPF is used as an inter-domain routing protocol

questions.explanation:
OSPF is a link-state protocol.

- "Uses Dijkstra" [latex]\text{---}[/latex] correct.
- "Inter-domain protocol": OSPF is intra-domain (inside one AS); BGP is inter-domain [latex]\text{---}[/latex] INCORRECT.
- "Hierarchical routing" with areas and a backbone [latex]\text{---}[/latex] correct.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

(i) Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) provides a mapping from an IP address to the corresponding hardware (link-layer) address.
(ii) A single TCP segment from a sender S to a receiver R cannot carry both data from S to R and acknowledgement for a segment from R to S.

Which ONE of the following is CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
(i) ARP maps IP addresses to hardware (MAC) addresses: this is exactly ARP's definition — TRUE.

(ii) "A single TCP segment cannot carry both data and an acknowledgement": this is FALSE. TCP is full-duplex, and a very common optimization called piggybacking lets a single outgoing segment simultaneously carry new data (from S to R) and an acknowledgement field (ACKing previously received data from R) — the TCP header always has an ACK field available regardless of whether the segment also carries data.

Answer: (i) is TRUE and (ii) is FALSE

Click here for detail solution

questions.question: Suppose that the stop-and-wait protocol is used on a link with a bit rate of 64 kilobits per second and 20 milliseconds propagation delay. Assume that the transmission time for the acknowledgement and the processing time at nodes are negligible. Then the minimum frame size in bytes to achieve a link utilization of at least 50% is______________.
questions.explanation:
Stop-and-wait utilization = [latex]\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}\ge\frac12\Rightarrow T_t\ge2T_p=40[/latex] ms.

Frame size = [latex]64\times10^3\times40\times10^{-3}=2560[/latex] bits = 320 bytes.

Answer: 320

questions.question:
A graphical HTML browser resident at a network client machine Q accesses a static HTML
webpage from a HTTP server S. The static HTML page has exactly one static embedded
image which is also at S. Assuming no caching, which one of the following is correct about
the HTML webpage loading (including the embedded image)?

options.A:
Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, each necessarily in a separate TCP
connection to server S
options.B: Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, but a single TCP connection to server S is sufficient
options.C: A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and a single TCP connection between Q and S is necessary for this
options.D: A single HTTP request from Q to S is sufficient, and this is possible without any TCP connection between Q and S

questions.explanation:
The HTML page and the embedded image are two separate objects, so at least 2 HTTP GET requests are needed.

With persistent HTTP (keep-alive), both requests can be sent over one TCP connection.

Answer: Q needs to send at least 2 HTTP requests to S, but a single TCP connection is sufficient

questions.question:
Consider two hosts P and Q connected through a router R. The maximum transfer unit (MTU) value of the link between P and R is 1500 bytes, and between R and Q is 820 bytes.
A TCP segment of size 1400 bytes was transferred from P to Q through R, with IP identification value as 0x1234. Assume that the IP header size is 20 bytes. Further, the packet is allowed to be fragmented, i.e., Don't Fragment (DF) flag in the IP header is not set by P.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.A: Two fragments are created at R and the IP datagram size carrying the second fragment is 620 bytes.
options.B: If the second fragment is lost, R will resend the fragment with the IP identification value 0x1234.
options.C: If the second fragment is lost, P is required to resend the whole TCP segment.
options.D: TCP destination port can be determined by analysing only the second fragment.

questions.explanation:
P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R: 1400 + 20 = 1420 [latex]\le[/latex] 1500, no fragmentation. R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q (MTU 820): max data 800 (a multiple of 8).
- Fragments: 800 and 600 bytes of data [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] datagrams of 820 and 620 bytes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Routers do not keep or resend fragments [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- IP cannot rebuild the datagram without the lost piece; TCP at P must resend the whole segment [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- The TCP header (with ports) is only in the first fragment [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

questions.question:
Consider a network with 6 routers R1 to R6 connected with links having weights as shown in the following diagram

All the routers use the distance vector based routing algorithm to update their routing tables. Each router starts with its routing table initialized to contain an entry for each neighbour with the weight of the respective connecting link. After all the routing tables stabilize, how many links in the network will never be used for carrying any data?
questions.explanation:
Check each link against the alternative path:
- R1-R2 (6): R1-R3-R2 = 3 + 2 = 5 is shorter [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] unused
- R4-R6 (8): R4-R5-R6 = 1 + 4 = 5 is shorter [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] unused
- R3-R5 (9) is still better than R3-R2-R4-R5 = 10, and the other links are on shortest paths

Answer: 2

questions.question:
Consider a network with 6 routers R1 to R6 connected with links having weights as shown in the following diagram

Suppose the weights of all unused links in the previous question are changed to 2 and the distance vector algorithm is used again until all routing tables stabilize. How many links will now remain unused?
questions.explanation:
Now R1-R2 = 2 and R4-R6 = 2.

- R5-R6 (4): R5-R4-R6 = 1 + 2 = 3 is shorter, and no shortest path uses R5-R6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] unused
- R1-R3 (3 vs 4 via R2) and R3-R5 (9 vs 10 via R2, R4) are still used, as are all other links

Answer: 1

questions.question: An ISP having an address block [latex]202.16.0.0/15[/latex] assigns a block of [latex]6000[/latex] IP addresses to a client, using the classless internet domain routing (CIDR) super-netting approach. Which of the following address blocks can be assigned by the ISP?
questions.explanation:
The ISP's block [latex]202.16.0.0/15[/latex] spans two full class-B-sized blocks: all addresses from [latex]202.16.0.0[/latex] to [latex]202.17.255.255[/latex].

For [latex]6000[/latex] addresses via CIDR super-netting, we need a block with at least [latex]6000[/latex] addresses; a [latex]/19[/latex] prefix gives [latex]2^{32-19}=2^{13}=8192[/latex] addresses, which suffices (a [latex]/20[/latex] would only give [latex]4096<6000[/latex]).

A valid [latex]/19[/latex] sub-block must (a) lie entirely within [latex]202.16.0.0[/latex]-[latex]202.17.255.255[/latex], and (b) have its network address aligned to a multiple of [latex]32[/latex] in the relevant octet (since [latex]/19[/latex] leaves [latex]13[/latex] host bits, and [latex]2^{13}=8192=32\times256[/latex] addresses per block, so the 3rd octet must be a multiple of [latex]32[/latex]: [latex]0,32,64,\ldots[/latex]).

- [latex]202.16.0.0/19[/latex]: [latex]0[/latex] is a valid multiple of [latex]32[/latex], and within range. Valid.
- [latex]202.17.64.0/19[/latex]: [latex]64[/latex] is a valid multiple of [latex]32[/latex], [latex]202.17.x[/latex] is within the /15 range. Valid.
- [latex]202.16.32.0/19[/latex]: [latex]32[/latex] is a valid multiple of [latex]32[/latex]. Valid.
- [latex]202.17.24.0/19[/latex]: [latex]24[/latex] is not a multiple of [latex]32[/latex] (valid boundaries are [latex]0,32,64,\ldots[/latex]), so this is not a properly aligned [latex]/19[/latex] block. Invalid.

Answer: 202.16.0.0/19, 202.17.64.0/19, and 202.16.32.0/19 can be assigned.

Click here for detail solution

questions.question:
Consider a selective repeat sliding window protocol that uses a frame size of 1 KB to send
data on a 1.5 Mbps link with a one-way latency of 50 msec. To achieve a link utilization of
60%, the minimum number of bits required to represent the sequence number field is ________.
questions.explanation:
Frame time = 8192 / 1.5 Mbps [latex]\approx[/latex] 5.46 ms; one cycle = 5.46 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 50 = 105.46 ms.
For 60% utilization: [latex]W\times5.46=0.6\times105.46\Rightarrow W\approx11.6[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 12 frames.

Selective repeat needs [latex]2^{k-1}\ge12\Rightarrow k=5[/latex] bits.

Answer: 5

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question:
Consider a source computer (S) transmitting a file of size [latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits to a destination computer (D)
over a network of two routers (R1 and R2) and three links (L1, L2, and L3). L1 connects S to R1; L2
connects R1 to R2; and L3 connects R2 to D. Let each link be of length 100 km. Assume signals
travel over each link at a speed of [latex]10^{8}[/latex] meters per second. Assume that the link bandwidth on each
link is 1Mbps. Let the file be broken down into 1000 packets each of size 1000 bits. Find the total
sum of transmission and propagation delays in transmitting the file from S to D?
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Per packet: [latex]T_t=\frac{1000}{10^6}=1[/latex] ms; per link: [latex]T_p=\frac{10^5}{10^8}=1[/latex] ms
- Packets are pipelined: the source sends all 1000 packets in 1000 ms. The last packet then needs 2 more transmissions (at R1, R2) and 3 propagations.

Total = 1000 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 1005 ms

Answer: 1005 ms

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question: Every host in an IPv4 network has a 1-second resolution real-time clock with battery backup. Each host needs to generate up to 1000 unique identifiers per second. Assume that each host has a globally unique IPv4 address. Design a 50-bit globally unique ID for this purpose. After what period (in seconds) will the identifiers generated by a host wrap around?
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- IPv4 address (global uniqueness): 32 bits
- Up to 1000 IDs per second: 10 bits ([latex]2^{10}=1024[/latex])
- Remaining for the clock: 50 [latex]-[/latex] 32 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 8 bits

The clock part repeats after [latex]2^8=256[/latex] seconds.

Answer: 256

questions.question:
An IP machine Q has a path to another IP machine H via three IP routers R1, R2, and R3.
Q---R1---R2---R3---H
H acts as an HTTP server, and Q connects to H via HTTP and downloads a file. Session layer encryption is used, with DES as the shared key encryption protocol. Consider the following four pieces of information:
[I1] The URL of the file downloaded by Q
[I2] The TCP port numbers at Q and H
[I3] The IP addresses of Q and H
[I4] The link layer addresses of Q and H
Which of I1, I2, I3, and I4 can an intruder learn through sniffing at R2 alone?
questions.explanation:
Session-layer encryption hides everything above the session layer (the HTTP request, so the URL I1 is hidden).

- TCP header (ports, I2) and IP header (addresses of Q and H, I3) are below it and travel in clear [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] visible at R2.
- Link layer addresses change at every hop; at R2 the frame carries the MACs of R1/R2/R3, not of Q and H [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] I4 not visible.

Answer: Only I2 and I3

questions.question:
Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window
of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet
loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip
Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the
third RTT will be _________

Answer: 4

questions.question:
Suppose we are transmitting frames between two nodes using the Stop-and-Wait protocol. The frame size is 3000 bits. The transmission rate of the channel is 2000 bps (bits/second) and the propagation delay between the two nodes is 100 milliseconds. Assume that the processing times at the source and destination are negligible. Also, assume that the size of the acknowledgment packet is negligible.  
Which ONE of the following most accurately gives the channel utilization for the above scenario in percentage?
questions.explanation:
Transmission time [latex]T_t=\dfrac{3000\text{ bits}}{2000\text{ bps}}=1.5[/latex] s. Propagation delay [latex]T_p=0.1[/latex] s (one-way).

In Stop-and-Wait, the sender must wait a full round trip (plus negligible ack transmission/processing time) after sending each frame before sending the next:
Utilization [latex]=\dfrac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}=\dfrac{1.5}{1.5+0.2}=\dfrac{1.5}{1.7}\approx0.8823=88.23\%[/latex]

Answer: 88.23
